correctness.rationale: For each m>=3 in H_m={x:sum x_i=1} with the inherited Euclidean metric, the half-spaces x_i<=2x_j have centered normals Π(e_i-2e_j) of squared norm 5-1/m, all genuine facets, so the centered John radius squared is 1/[m(5m-1)]. Kazakov’s listed vertices v_L have k low coordinates 1/(2m-k) and remaining 2/(2m-k); direct exact squared distance is k(m-k)/[m(2m-k)^2]. The derivative m(2m-3x)/(2m-x)^3 plus exact adjacent-cardinality comparisons proves the unique maximizing k: 2q when m=3q, otherwise 2q+1. S_m irreducibility on the sum-zero hyperplane makes the unique John/Löwner ellipsoids centered balls. Explicit zero-first-moment isotropic frame identities for ALL facet normals and the unique contact vertex orbit certify global ellipsoid optimality, not merely maximal centered balls. Independently recomputed exact ratios for m=3..25 and full rational facet Gram frames for m=3..8; finite checks corroborate the symbolic all-m proof.
